Preserved archive and public source allow independent inspection

Execute the automated test suite
Change backup age, ownership, or restore-test dates and verify the resulting finding changes deterministically
project-recovery.html.limitations: This audits declared recovery evidence; it does not execute a restore, prove data integrity, or establish business acceptance of a recovered service.

Introduce a dependency edge or cycle
Compare the resulting impact paths and recovery order to the expected graph reasoning
project-dependency.html.limitations: A graph can only be as accurate as its declared edges; real production dependencies require observation and owner validation.

project-cache-consistency-lab.html.title: Cache Consistency & Stampede Lab
project-cache-consistency-lab.html.evidence: Cache-aside baseline, hot-key invalidation scenario, single-flight mitigation, and origin-load metrics
project-cache-consistency-lab.html.problem: Caching can move failure from latency to consistency or overload. The lab exposes stale-read, invalidation, and thundering-herd tradeoffs.
constraints: Synthetic cache/origin model
Freshness policy must be explicit
Concurrent misses should not overwhelm the origin
architecture: Single-flight request coalescing for hot misses
verification: Hot-key invalidation increases origin load without coalescing
Single-flight collapses concurrent misses
Freshness and hit ratio remain visible
reproduce: Run baseline cache state
Invalidate the hot key
Enable single-flight and compare origin requests
project-cache-consistency-lab.html.limitations: The lab does not model a real distributed cache, network partitions, or multi-region consistency protocol.

project-progressive-delivery-control-pla.title: Progressive Delivery Control Plane
project-progressive-delivery-control-pla.evidence: Canary cohorts, SLO threshold, degradation scenario, staged promotion, and automated rollback decision
project-progressive-delivery-control-pla.problem: A deployment should be judged by runtime evidence before its blast radius expands. The lab models canary progression as a controlled decision process.
constraints: Synthetic release telemetry
SLO guardrails must control promotion
Rollback must be automatic when the canary violates policy
verification: Healthy canary is held/advanced within policy
Degraded canary exceeds the SLO and triggers rollback
Decision is tied to visible metrics
reproduce: Run baseline canary
Degrade the canary
Advance a healthy rollout and compare traffic/error metrics
project-progressive-delivery-control-pla.limitations: This does not deploy real workloads or integrate with a production GitOps/mesh platform.

project-mini-compiler-static-analyzer.ht.title: Mini Compiler & Static Analyzer
project-mini-compiler-static-analyzer.ht.evidence: Tokenizer, parser/type-checker model, valid program, type-error scenario, and source-oriented diagnostics
project-mini-compiler-static-analyzer.ht.problem: Compiler construction forces software semantics to be explicit. The lab demonstrates how tokens, syntax trees, types, and diagnostics compose into a correctness pipeline.
constraints: Small educational language
Errors should be found before execution when statically decidable
Diagnostics must identify the source construct involved
verification: Valid numeric program produces zero type errors
STRING + NUMBER is rejected
Token/source locations remain visible
reproduce: Compile the valid sample
Introduce the type error
Inspect tokens and the resulting type-check failure
project-mini-compiler-static-analyzer.ht.limitations: The current lab is a compact compiler model; it does not yet generate bytecode/native code or implement full scopes/control flow.

project-reliable-message-processing.html.title: Reliable Message Processing & Transactional Outbox Lab
project-reliable-message-processing.html.evidence: At-least-once delivery model, duplicate-delivery scenario, idempotent-consumer mitigation, and outbox state
project-reliable-message-processing.html.problem: Distributed message delivery is often at-least-once, so consumers must be designed for duplicate delivery and database/publish failure boundaries.
constraints: At-least-once delivery semantics
Duplicate effects must be suppressed explicitly
Database state and message publication must not rely on an unsafe dual write
verification: Duplicate delivery exposes duplicate-side-effect risk
Idempotency suppresses repeated effects
Outbox state keeps persistence/publication boundary visible
reproduce: Run baseline message processing
Redeliver a message
Enable idempotency/outbox protection and compare outcomes
project-reliable-message-processing.html.limitations: The lab does not connect to a real broker or database and does not claim exactly-once transport semantics.
